before: A historically anchored programme combines all six available UCR History courses with three art-history courses on Renaissance-to-modern visual culture, early-modern global connections and historiography. Economics, sociology, political thought and international relations supply complementary explanations of institutions, inequality and change; quantitative and qualitative methods support inquiry. The final History seminar researches primary sources from the 1809 Walcheren Expedition. This is sustained historical study, but it does not reproduce Erasmus’s complete economic-history focus area, philosophy-of-history course, individual thesis or internship.
after: A historically anchored programme combines all six available UCR History courses with three art-history courses on Renaissance-to-modern visual culture, early-modern global connections and historiography. Economics, sociology, political thought and international relations supply complementary explanations of institutions, inequality and change; quantitative and qualitative methods support inquiry. The final History seminar develops historical questions, critical source engagement and a substantial research paper in Researching the American Century. This is sustained historical study, but it does not reproduce Erasmus’s complete economic-history focus area, philosophy-of-history course, individual thesis or internship.
